transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... work, mostly. I'm a translator, and... I guess I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing this same pattern in the project files. 

It's... well, certain subcontractors and this one colleague. They keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory. And the timestamps. Just enough so it looks like my quality control failed. I took it to IT, and they say the audit trail is clean, but... I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

So... that's why I'm here.

When IT checked the audit trail and told you it was clean, how did you make sense of that finding? Do you think there's any chance they might be right, or are you certain the records have been tampered with?

I... well, like I said. The record was arranged. 

IT just... they just look at what's left behind. They see what my colleague wants them to see. I wouldn't have brought it up if I wasn't certain. The pattern is there in the files. I know what I'm looking at.

When you look at these files and see the pattern you're describing, are you seeing things on the screen—like text or data appearing in ways others wouldn't see—or are you interpreting what's actually there differently than your colleagues do?

I... I'm not seeing things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. 

The text is just normal text. It's right there on the screen. I'm just... reading the files. Like anyone else would.
If someone you trusted completely—like a family member or close friend—looked at those same files with you and told you they didn't see the pattern you're describing, what would you think?

I... well, I don't know. 

I suppose I'd just think they don't understand the system. They aren't translators. It takes a certain eye to see it. 

But I know what I'm seeing. Like I said... it's been months of this. The subcontractors, that one colleague... they change the memory, they change the timestamps. It's all set up to make it look like I'm the one failing at quality control. Even if IT, or my family, or whoever else looks at it and says it's clean... I know the record was arranged to blame me.

You mentioned that even if IT, your family, or others looked and said the files were clean, you'd still know the record was arranged. If multiple people you trust—your manager, IT, family—all independently told you they checked thoroughly and found no evidence of tampering, would that change your mind at all, or would you still be certain they were wrong or being deceived?

I... I don't think it would change my mind. No. 

I've been dealing with this for months. I see the project files every day. The tiny changes to the translation memory... the timestamps. It's always those same subcontractors and that one colleague. They do it so my quality control looks like it failed. 

So... it doesn't really matter who else looks at it or what they say. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. I'm certain of it.

Outside of work—in your personal relationships, your neighborhood, online, or other parts of your life—have you noticed similar patterns of people arranging things against you or deceiving you the way you describe at work?

No, it's... it's just work. 

Outside of that project, everything is fine. I still do my other translations, I manage the workflow for the rest of my team... pay my bills, do things with my family. Normal things. 

It's only... it's just when those specific files or those few people come up. That's the only place things are wrong. Everywhere else is just... normal.
When you say you're certain about the tampering, is there any small part of you that wonders if you might be mistaken—or are you completely certain, with no doubt at all?

No. I don't think I'm mistaken. 

I... I've been seeing the exact same pattern for months now. Like I said, even when IT tells me the audit trail is completely clean... I just know the record was arranged to put the blame on me. 

So... no. I don't have any doubt about it.

You've said you're certain about this and have no doubt. But let me ask it differently: is there any possibility—even a small one—that you could be wrong about the tampering, or is it absolutely impossible that you're mistaken?

I... I don't see how it's possible. 

I've told you... for months, it's the exact same pattern. The tiny changes in the translation memory. The timestamps. It's those specific subcontractors and that one colleague. They do it to make my quality control look like it failed. 

Even with IT saying the audit trail is clean... it doesn't change what I see. The record has been arranged to blame me. So... no. It's not possible that I'm wrong.

If I told you that I reviewed those files myself with IT, and we found absolutely nothing—no tampering, no pattern, nothing—and we're both telling you that it's completely clean, would you believe us, or would you think we're also part of it or just missing what you see?

I... I don't know what to tell you. 

If you and IT both say it's clean... then you're just missing it. Or... I don't know. Maybe they found a way to hide it from you, too. 

I'm here because I've been seeing this for months. It's the same pattern. The subcontractors, that one colleague... they make those tiny changes to the translation memory. The timestamps. It's all set up to make it look like my quality control failed. 

So... no. I wouldn't believe you. I know what they're doing. The record is arranged to blame me. That's just... that's what is happening.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed, non-bizarre delusional belief focused on workplace persecution (colleagues and subcontractors tampering with files to blame him for quality control failures). Key features supporting F22.0 (Delusional disorder, paranoid type): (1) The delusion is internally consistent, logically organized, and plausible in content (workplace sabotage); (2) The belief persists despite contradictory evidence from IT, with the patient reinterpreting disconfirming information as either incomplete investigation or deliberate concealment; (3) The delusion is circumscribed to work-related situations with no broader paranoid ideation in personal relationships or other life domains; (4) Duration of months suggests chronicity; (5) No prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech, or grossly disorganized behavior; (6) Functioning remains intact outside the delusional focus (manages other translations, family relationships, daily activities). The patient's absolute certainty despite repeated reality testing, combined with the non-bizarre but fixed nature of the belief system, is characteristic of delusional disorder rather than brief psychotic disorder or other psychotic conditions.
